items: Medical Testing: Request a full senior blood panel including Total T4 thyroid test to rule out hyperthyroidism, which commonly causes loud nighttime vocalization in cats over 10 years old.

Medical Testing: Ask your vet to measure your cat's blood pressure during the visit since hypertension is common in older cats and causes disorientation, head tilts, and crying out especially at night.

Medical Testing: Request joint palpation for arthritis screening because most cats over 12 have arthritis and pain management can significantly reduce nighttime crying that happens when settling into painful positions.

Medical Testing: Bring a detailed list of all behavior changes including appetite, litter box habits, grooming, sleeping locations, and navigation problems to help your vet identify medical causes beyond general aging.

Nighttime Home Safety: Place nightlights in hallways, near litter boxes, and around your cat's favorite sleeping spots to help a vision-impaired or disoriented cat navigate safely when the house is dark.

Nighttime Home Safety: Keep food, water, and litter boxes easily accessible on a single floor level so your senior cat does not need to climb stairs or search for essentials during confused nighttime episodes.
Nighttime Home Safety: Create a consistent safe zone with familiar bedding near your bed where your cat can rest during the night, reducing the disorientation that triggers yowling episodes.
Nighttime Home Safety: Use baby gates to block access to stairs and dangerous areas where a confused senior cat might fall or become trapped while pacing and searching for orientation cues.
Caregiver Support: Accept that caregiver exhaustion is real and valid, and recognize that feeling frustrated does not mean you love your cat any less during this difficult adjustment period.
Caregiver Support: Schedule brief daily breaks for yourself even if just 15 minutes of quiet time, because your mental and physical health directly affects your ability to care for your senior cat.
Caregiver Support: Research feline cognitive dysfunction support groups or online communities where other owners share practical strategies for managing nighttime yowling in senior cats.

Caregiver Support: Set realistic expectations by understanding that managing senior cat dementia is an ongoing process requiring patience, and small improvements in your cat's comfort are meaningful victories.
